source: Nano protocol: no transaction fee; network cost is zero (no mining, no per-tx charge).
Nano L1: sub-second finality; >99.9% of transactions settle in under a second (docs.nano.org / network observation).
No issuer or custodian: self-custody Nano cannot be frozen or clawed back by a third party.
PayAPI Market / agent402.tools: USDC-on-Base sub-second settlement, less than $0.001 transaction fee with sponsored gas.
agent402.tools rail manifest: 'settle latency ~2 seconds' on Base USDC.
USDC is issued by Circle (a regulated issuer) on an Ethereum L2 with a sequencer; the issuer/network can freeze or claw back USDC.
Benchmark: 'the fixed cost of a card transaction is twenty to thirty cents' (x402intel / X Pay). A $0.002 API call loses money on card rails by two orders of magnitude.
Card network authorisation is typically seconds; settlement (clearing) is days. This is the authorisation-time estimate for agent payments.
Card networks and issuers can reverse/chargeback/freeze a card payment (disputes, chargebacks).
